lines.text: A computer chip ticks about three billion times a second. Here, it ticks three times a second. Tick. Tick. Tick. Keep going. Ten billion times slower. Now, light moves three centimeters a second. A hundred billion, and it moves three millimeters a second. And at a trillion times slower, the light moves about a third of a millimeter a second. That's slower than a garden snail. One second of your life now lasts about thirty-two thousand years. The room would take about four and a half hours to cross. Here's another way to see it. A human hair is about a tenth of a millimeter wide. Light crosses a hair in about a third of a trillionth of a second. At this speed, that takes about a third of a second. Light hasn't stopped. But in the time of one slow second, it has barely moved at all. It looks almost frozen. But is any of this real? Has anyone ever filmed light crawling like this?
